rc4.txt, aes128.txt, aes256.txt and bp.txt come from the public captures of the
archive.org item dmr-encrypted-samples_202511 ("Dmr Encrypted Samples.zip", SHA-256
944fe9af0b8949fe18f25b60238f24c0068c21e52aac966d933cfa9316dd5447, uploaded 2025-11-13,
Public Domain Mark 1.0), fetched on 2026-10-26: RC4-40.wav, AES-128.wav, AES-256.wav and
MOTO-BP.wav, 48 kHz discriminator audio. The item publishes the keys: 40-bit 373374ABE8,
128-bit 373374ABE8E9D13AA90900B9A3101664, 256-bit
3AF8C96E21BEFDE927EE1D03DF53CFA701516B0642AC7B38643549E2BE79840E, and Basic Privacy key
number 100.

dsd-fme (lwvmobile/dsd-fme, branch audio_work, build AW 2026-55-g72b3e5e) decoded each
file twice with -fs -Z, without the key and with it (-1, -H, or -4 -b 100). Line "pi" is
the PI header payload that it printed (12 octets with the CRC), line "lc" the Voice LC
Header payload (12 octets with the RS parity; for bp.txt the 9 octets of the embedded LC,
as that file has no header). Each other line is one AMBE+2 frame in call order, the 49
bits packed as vocoder.AMBEFrame: the frame as received, then the frame that dsd-fme
printed with the key.

MOTO-BP.wav sets neither the Privacy service option nor FID 0x10 in its LC. Every frame
of bp.txt differs from its clear frame by 450245624562 then 7 zero bits, the pattern of
the 16-bit value 0x4562.

data-rc4.txt is the encrypted data packet of the comment of 2026-10-22 by the dsd-fme
author on lwvmobile/dsd-fme issue 372 ("Hytera Encrypted PDU Support", fetched
2026-10-26): a Hytera radio sending a UTF-16BE text message with DMRA RC4, key
1234567890, key ID 1, MI 0C01A418, as dsd-fme printed it. Line "header" is the first
header (U_HEAD, SAP 9), "phead" the P_HEAD, "block" each rate 1/2 data block, each 12
octets with its CRC. Line "plain" is the user data that dsd-fme printed with the key,
"clear" the user data of the same message sent without encryption, from the same issue;
the two differ only in octet 0, the IPv4 identification of the compressed header. The
message CRC of the encrypted packet is that of the encrypted user data.
The P_HEADs of TestDataCaptureHeaderVariants come from the logs that the dsd-fme author
posted on lwvmobile/dsd-fme issues 283 and 357 (RC4 privacy headers with key IDs 7 and
1, an MNIS header) and 372 (a Hytera header, MFID 0x68). Their CRCs hold. The Basic
Privacy headers of those issues come from RAS systems, whose header CRC the logs do not
show unmasked, so the tests leave them out.

Search for encrypted DMR data captures with a known key, 2026-10-26:
- archive.org: advanced search for DMR with encrypted, encryption, rc4, aes, privacy,
  sample, capture and recording; the uploader and creator of dmr-encrypted-samples_202511
  (one item, voice only); dmr-cracker (an RC4 key finder, no captures).
- lwvmobile/dsd-fme issues: 372 (the RC4 data capture above, and Hytera BP data with keys
  1234567890 and ABCDEF1234), 283 and 357 (encryption headers without keys), 194 (RC4
  text message captures offered by a user, shared in private), 79, 296 (RC4 voice MP3s
  with key 1234567ABC), 314, 316, 319, 321, 356, 360. The source files dmr_block.c and
  dmr_pi.c (data and voice layouts, for cross-checking only).
- arancormonk/dsd-neo: issues and pull requests on encrypted PDUs (3, 35, 337, 342, 353,
  496, 498, 550, 746, 762), the test tree (tests/protocol/dmr/test_dmr_block_crypto.c holds
  synthetic AES and RC4 data cases, not captures; tests/crypto holds cipher tests).
- DSheirer/sdrtrunk issues (6, 1269, 2376): no encrypted data samples.
- OK-DMR/ok-dmrlib 1.x (installed copy): privacy flags only, no encrypted data.
- tylerwatt12/known-key-mbe-samples and MattCheramie/GopherTrunk issues 1187 and 1195:
  known-key captures of voice only.
- gophertrunk.org/reference/dmr-encryption and gophertrunk.org/dmr-encryption.html:
  voice only.
- sigidwiki.com Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) and its talk page: one ARC4 voice sample, no
  key, no data.
- RadioReference forum threads: "Using DSD-FME to Decode Encrypted DMR Samples" (the
  archive.org voice set), "Request Anytone DMR Arc40 Captures" and the DSD FME thread
  page 38 (voice), "Sample of DMR with basic privacy recorded with sdr" (a request), "Is
  this Basic, Enhanced or AES Encryption", "Mototrbo Enhanced and Basic Privacy
  question", "MOTOTRBO / DMR: Privacy from competitors listening?": no data with keys.
- brmlab.cz DMR project, cryptomuseum.com DMR, the md380tools group thread "Mototrbo
  Basic Privacy Key", the MOTOTRBO privacy wiki (cwh050): descriptions, no captures.
- Moto.Net (pboyd04), named in issue 194: its Encrypter is the XNL login of the
  network protocol, not air privacy; no captures. node-dmr-lib (rick51231),
  src/Encryption/ARC4.js: the same ARC4 keying (key, then the 4 MI octets, 256 octets
  dropped), which agrees with this package; no captures.
- Academic papers: none found that publishes DMR data captures with keys.
No public capture with a key exists for AES data, DES data or Basic Privacy data.

Basic Privacy key numbers: the spot checks of TestBasicKeyNumber for numbers other than
208 to 223 are entries of the table in include/bp.h of dsd-fme (audio_work, ISC), which
equal the XOR rule of NewBasicKeyNumber for 240 of its 256 entries. For 208 to 223 the
test holds the rule values; the table differs there. The captures test runs bp.txt with
NewBasicKeyNumber(100), the key number that the archive.org item names.
